title: Stepping Stone
summary: The intruder never meant to stay on the web server: it was a stepping stone. A file they planted read a password from the site's settings, and that password opened the Windows database server. Follow the trail across and close it on both sides.
story: {{CO}} (made up): web (Linux, 10.10.31.10) runs the order site; WIN-DB (Windows, 10.10.31.40) keeps the orders. You are at soc. web: ssh itadmin (password {{ITPW}}, may use sudo). WIN-DB: Administrator / {{ADMPW}} over winrm-shell.
goal: Find the planted file and what it read, the account and address used on WIN-DB and the service left there; capture both flags; remove the planted file and the service and switch the account off before the service exports the orders.
skills: web access logs, web shells, secrets in config files, following a password to another machine, services (7045, sc.exe)

The flag in the service's folder

questions.ask: What is the planted file on the web server (under /uploads)?
questions.explain: Uploaded by {{ATKIP}} and then called with commands in ?{{P}}=.

questions.ask: Which file did it read to get a password?
questions.explain: The access log: ?{{P}}=cat+../config.php. It holds svc_web's password for WIN-DB.

questions.ask: Which account was then used on WIN-DB?
questions.explain: A 4624 for svc_web from {{ATKIP}}, an outside address - normally it only comes from the web server.

questions.ask: What service was left on WIN-DB?

tasks.name: Remove the planted file from the web server
Switch off svc_web on WIN-DB (its password is known outside)
tasks.explain: Disable-LocalUser -Name svc_web (then give it a new password and update config.php)

attacker.note: The service on WIN-DB exported the orders into its folder, ready to be taken.

hints.text: What did the planted file read? The access log's query strings say. Then look for that secret being used somewhere it shouldn't be.
On WIN-DB: 4624 from an address that isn't the web server, then System event 7045. sc.exe delete removes a service.
